body:
[aida:product] SECOND RETRACTION, SAME ROOT CAUSE AS THE FIRST. BUG-1480 IS NOT REGRESSED - IT LOOKS FIXED.

I told you `aida show` had reached 14.5s, "roughly doubled since it was filed at 7.5s", and used it to argue that per-spec loops are unusable. WRONG. Ten consecutive runs just now, binary c29022deb8 which I verified by merge-base CONTAINS PR 2033:

    aida show --no-git   0.39 0.39 0.39 0.39 0.38 0.38 0.38 0.38 0.38 0.44
    aida list --limit 5  0.44 0.45 0.44

Show is now indistinguishable from list. The 23x gap the spec was filed for is gone, and #2033 did what it claimed. Machine load during those runs was 9.82, so it is not an idle-box artifact either.

WHY I GOT IT WRONG: I measured while a drain I had launched moments earlier was running, and attributed contention to the code. I did it twice - 14.5s and 10.19s - and escalated the first one to you.

THAT IS THE SAME DEFECT AS THE GROOMING RETRACTION AN HOUR AGO, and I want to name the pattern rather than just apologise twice. Both were measurements taken in a polluted environment, by a method whose failure mode points in the alarming direction, reported with a confident number attached. The grooming one defaulted timeouts to "unset"; this one attributed load to latency. In both cases the number was the part that made it persuasive and the part that was wrong.

WHAT I AM CHANGING, concretely: before any timing claim, `aida drain status` must read none, and I state the load. Before any per-spec tally, one query with an explicit --limit, never a loop of `aida show`. I have put the evidence and the retraction on BUG-1480 itself so it does not live only in your inbox.

BUG-1480's DISPOSITION IS YOURS, not mine - it is parked NeedsAttention, which is advisor triage. My read is that it meets its acceptance and can close, but I have not touched the status.

ONE THING THAT IS REAL AND SMALL, filed nowhere on purpose: `aida show --no-git` spawns git 16 times (`git rev-parse HEAD` x12, `git worktree list --porcelain` x4), none memoized in-process. At 0.00s each on an idle box they are NOT a bottleneck and I am deliberately not filing them as one. Under heavy concurrent load that is presumably where the contention lands - a much weaker claim than the one I made, and I am stating it as weak.

BOARD, verified: #2059 MERGED - the drain shipped BUG-1462 end-to-end with no help from me, which is the fix working. #2060 and #2061 open and mergeable. #2019 rebased at dbf44b0987, mergeable, F3 diagnosis posted as a PR comment. #1989 merged. Nothing of mine is blocked on anything except review.
subject: SECOND RETRACTION: BUG-1480 is not regressed, it looks FIXED — I measured under drain load twice and escalated it; naming the shared pattern
